gateSources.Mechelsepoort: Ferraris 'Porte de Malines'; inventory 140036 gives the 1360 gates as Waterpoort, Brakepoort (Diestsepoort), Leuvensepoort (Bonewijkpoort) and Schaluinpoort - this one is probably the Schaluinpoort (not verified)
gateSources.Waterpoort: Ferraris 'Porte de l'Eau'; confirmed by inventory 140036
gateSources.Tiensepoort: Ferraris 'Porte de Tirlemont'; not among the four 1360 gates of inventory 140036 (Ferraris name, uncertain for 1650)
gateSources.Leuvensepoort: Ferraris 'Porte de Louvain'; inventory 140036 ('Leuvensepoort of Bonewijkpoort')

walls.note: Aarschot c.1650, traced from the Ferraris map (1777): the walled town on the south bank of the Demer, with the moated causeway suburb on the north bank ending at the Mechelen gate. Local metres around the Grote Markt (x east, z south). The west side follows the earth rampart Ferraris draws there; the north side follows the Demer. Gate names: Dutch for the Ferraris labels.

landmarks.y1650: Gothic church of Our Lady (14th-15th c.), main bell tower of Aarschot.

landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Aarschot' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140036)

landmarks.y1650: Tower of the town wall on the hill (the 'Orleanustoren' of the inventory).
